title: Consensus of scholars
hook: agreement of the scholars as a source for Sunni schools

segments.voice: Yesterday: the sunnah as second, the Prophet's way that the book itself names. Your line: the sunnah explains.

What happens when the people who know a subject best all land in the same place? In Sunni legal thought, that landing place has a name, and it counts as a source of law in its own right, after the Qur'an and the sunnah. Not a vote. Not a poll of the public. The agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling. It sounds simple. Pinning down what it means, whose agreement counts, and how anyone could know it happened, kept scholars arguing. Today: ijma'.
screen: `EVERYONE LANDS IN ONE PLACE.` → `NOT A VOTE.` → `SIMPLE? NOT QUITE.`

segments.voice: Ijma' means agreement, a coming together on one thing. In Sunni legal theory it names the agreement of the qualified scholars of the community, in a given generation, on a ruling. The grounds? Scholars point to a report that the Prophet ﷺ said his community would not agree upon error. It comes in more than one collection, in different wordings, and critics have weighed its chains differently. Tradition says al-Shafi'i also pointed to a verse that warns against following a way other than the believers' way. What does consensus do? Where it exists, it settles a question. Scholars give examples like the obligation of the daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan, or the gathering of the Qur'an into one written copy that was passed on. And they hold that consensus rests on a text; it doesn't float free of the Qur'an and the sunnah. Then the arguments about agreement itself. Whose agreement counts? Only the companions'? The scholars of any generation? Imam Malik gave special weight to the practice of the people of Medina. Can a consensus even be known, once scholars live scattered across many lands? A saying attributed to Ahmad ibn Hanbal warns that someone who claims consensus may be speaking falsely, since people may have differed without his knowing. And Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus as proof when it reveals the view of the Imam, not as a source standing on its own. So agreement is itself a place where scholars disagree, carefully, which shows how much weight they gave it.
screen: `IJMA': A COMING TOGETHER.` · `WILL NOT AGREE UPON ERROR.` · `CONSENSUS RESTS ON A TEXT.` · `WHOSE AGREEMENT COUNTS?`

segments.voice: Take one ruling scholars give as an example of consensus: the fast of Ramadan is obligatory. Picture its reach, people of different schools, lands and languages, who differ on a great deal, all keeping the same month. Hold that picture for a few breaths.
Ijma'. Agreement: in Sunni law, the agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling, a source standing after the Qur'an and the sunnah. Today's word.
Your line: agreement. Not a vote, but the scholars landing in one place. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Sunni scholars treat a ruling on which the qualified scholars agreed as settled, while Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus when it reflects the view of the Imam; students learn which rulings are held to be agreed and which are differed over.

fork.setup: you're a scholar asked about a question, and you find that the scholars before you agreed on the answer. what do you do?
options: set their agreement aside and start from scratch.
treat the agreement as settling it, and look for the text it rests on.
put the question to a public vote.
fork.reveal: in Sunni legal theory, a real consensus settles the question, and it is expected to rest on a text. the hard part, scholars said, is knowing the agreement was real.

chat.says: Is ijma' basically Muslims voting on what the law should be?
options: No. It's the agreement of the qualified scholars on a ruling, resting on a text.
Yes. Whatever most Muslims agree on in a poll becomes part of the law.
No. It's one leading scholar's ruling, which everyone else then follows.
chat.meaning: Ijma' isn't a vote or a poll of the public. It's the qualified scholars landing in one place, resting on the Qur'an and sunnah.

ijma'.meaning: agreement: the qualified scholars' consensus on a ruling

al-Shafi'i.meaning: the scholar the Shafi'i school of law is named for

Ahmad ibn Hanbal.meaning: an early imam; the Hanbali school is named for him

Twelver Shia.meaning: Shia Muslims who follow twelve Imams of the Prophet's family

Medina.meaning: the Prophet's city, whose people's practice Malik weighed

sources.ref: Masa'il of Ahmad ibn Hanbal (narrated by his son Abdullah)

notes: 'My community will not agree upon error': Ibn Majah 3950 and Tirmidhi 2167 (wording 'Allah will not gather my ummah upon misguidance'); paraphrased and flagged as weighed differently. Confirm numbers.
Al-Shafi'i's use of Qur'an 4:115 for ijma' is given as 'tradition says' (al-Risala and the story of his search for a proof); confirm.
Examples of consensus (obligation of daily prayers and Ramadan fasting; the companions' agreement on the written mushaf) are standard examples; confirm. No numbers given.
'Consensus rests on a text' (the requirement of a mustanad) stated as what scholars hold; a Keeper may want 'most scholars'.
Malik and the practice ('amal) of Medina: described as 'special weight', not as ijma' proper; confirm the framing.
Ahmad's saying ('whoever claims consensus is lying; perhaps people differed') is attributed, paraphrased, and softened to 'may be speaking falsely'. Confirm source.
Twelver Shia view of ijma' as kashif (revealing the Imam's view): confirm wording. The outline's hook says 'a source for Sunni schools'; the Shia view is added for fairness.
Original: إجماع; pronunciation given as 'ij-MAA' (final 'ayn not marked); confirm.
